taxonomic_note: Accepted by Kew/POWO. Three accepted infraspecific taxa are preserved in review while the learner remains species-level.
look_here_first: First check the plant base and leaf tips. Drummond's skullcap is a small taprooted annual with visibly glandular-hairy stems/calyces; its leaves are acute-tipped, and lower stem leaves may be shallowly crenate. Then confirm the small blue-violet corolla and the visorlike Scutellaria calyx appendage.

project_inclusion.range_basis: BONAP/NAPA includes Scutellaria drummondii in its county-level Scutellaria atlas. Hays County — UT Plant Resources Center's Purola Preserve natural flora lists S. drummondii among naturally occurring plants. Travis County — UT Plant Resources Center's Travis County Lamiaceae specimen index includes S. drummondii var. drummondii and var. edwardsiana. Williamson County — UT Plant Resources Center publishes a dedicated Williamson County treatment for S. drummondii.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: The species includes multiple accepted varieties. The learner stays species-level and does not infer a variety from photographs unless diagnostic evidence supports it.

best_field_traits: annual, taprooted, usually 15–30 cm tall with one to several stems from the base
stems four-sided and densely short glandular-hairy
leaves opposite and decussate, generally ovate, with acute tips
lower cauline leaves shallowly crenate; upper leaves becoming entire
leafy raceme with paired opposite axillary flowers
pedicel very short at anthesis, about 1–1.2 mm
calyx two-lipped with the diagnostic projecting visorlike scutellum/appendage
calyx and scutellum visibly glandular short-pilose, often with longer marginal hairs
corolla about 5.5–10 mm long, blue-violet to blue; lower lip may have a white center with violet/blue spots
fruit produces four small tuberculate nutlets
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Scutellaria wrightii: S. wrightii is a bushy perennial with several-many stems from a persistent base, rounded/obtuse entire leaves, minute pubescence and a smoother-looking calyx; its corolla is larger (mostly 13–18 mm) and its pedicel longer (3–3.5 mm). S. drummondii is annual, acute-leaved, visibly glandular-hairy and smaller-flowered. Scutellaria ovata: S. ovata is a much taller rhizomatous perennial (about 35–70 cm in the Williamson treatment) with much larger triangular-ovate, crenate leaves and much larger corollas (about 21–25 mm).
